correctness.rationale: For each initial ordinal segment, noncofinal color classes are finitely many and bounded; their supremum defines a strictly smaller ordinal. Ordinal well-foundedness forces finite termination. The candidate atoms are definable inductively from Boolean valuation cells and Diamond of noncofinal portions. They generate a modal-stable Boolean algebra because every selected color is cofinal in its layer, making Diamond of a nonempty union an initial segment. Equality of these two subalgebras proves exact atomic partition and count for all ordinals, not merely finite test cases. Direct exhaustive finite closure computations confirm 6554 cases.

value.rationale: The precise structural question is to determine the generated modal algebra, not only to show its finiteness. A complete constructive atom normal form and exact size are given uniformly for all set ordinals and finite arities. The example of omega+1 shows genuinely new segment behavior beyond the omega analysis. Such exact finite quotients are natural for local-finiteness, finite model synthesis, and valuation-sensitive modal definability.
